cards.explanation: The answer is Judah, friends. The LORD answers, “Judah shall go up…” That's one name with no confusion. Most group chats need forty messages just to decide who's driving.

The answer is True. The LORD says, “Indeed, I have delivered the land into their hands.” That's before the first battle even starts. Judah still has to march up and fight, but they go knowing what the LORD has said.

The deal is that they fight with each other, friends. Judah says to their brothers the Simeonites, “Come up with us to our allotted territory, and let us fight against the Canaanites. And we likewise will go with you to your territory.” It's a swap. You help me, I help you, and everybody ends up with help.
The answer is False, friends. The text says, “So the Simeonites went with them.” Judah asks, and Simeon shows up. That's what brothers do.

The answer is False. Verse 4 says, “When Judah attacked, the LORD delivered the Canaanites and Perizzites into their hands…” Judah attacks, and the LORD is the One who delivers. Ten thousand men fall at Bezek, and the text gives the credit to Him.

The answer is that God has repaid him, friends. Adoni-bezek says, “As I have done to them, so God has repaid me.” I think this one is heavy. He is the one saying it, and he ties what happened to him to what he had done to seventy kings. We just hear him say it and move on.

The answer is capture, friends. Verse 8 says the men of Judah “…fought against Jerusalem and captured it.” The text goes on to say they put the city to the sword and set it on fire. That part is heavy, so I'll just say it plainly and keep going.

The answer is his daughter in marriage, friends. Caleb, one of Moses' spies (Numbers 13:6), says, “To the man who strikes down Kiriath-sepher and captures it, I will give my daughter Acsah in marriage.” He's offering a marriage to the man who captures the city.

The answer is Othniel, friends. He's the son of Caleb's younger brother Kenaz, so Caleb's nephew. The text says he captured the city, and Caleb gave him Acsah in marriage. Caleb said it, Othniel did it, and a deal is a deal.

The answer is springs of water, friends. Acsah says, “Since you have given me land in the Negev, give me springs of water as well.” I think she knows land is better with water. That's like me having a bakery with a lovely counter and no oven. Caleb gives her both the upper and lower springs.
The answer is False, friends. The text says, “So Caleb gave her both the upper and lower springs.” She asked for springs, and he gives her both. I think that's a happy ending for Acsah.

The answer is the descendants of Moses' father-in-law, friends. The text says the descendants of Moses' father-in-law, the Kenite, went up with the men of Judah. Moses, Israel's leader (Exodus 3:10), is the link. They went to live among the people.

The answer is Hormah, friends. After Judah and the Simeonites attack Zephath and devote the city to destruction, the text says, “So it was called Hormah.” The city goes from Zephath to Hormah in a single verse. My sign out front takes a whole weekend and a ladder.

The answer is True, friends. Verse 19 says, “The LORD was with Judah, and they took possession of the hill country…” That's the good news. The rest of the verse brings a hard part, but the hill country is theirs.

The answer is chariots of iron, friends. The verse says the LORD was with Judah, and they took possession of the hill country, “but they could not drive out the inhabitants of the plains because they had chariots of iron.” That's the reason the text gives, and it gives no other.
The answer is Caleb, friends. The text says, “Just as Moses had promised, Judah gave Hebron to Caleb…” Moses made the promise, and Judah kept it. A promise kept is a beautiful thing.

The answer is True, friends. The verse says Caleb “…drove out the descendants of the three sons of Anak.” Earlier, Judah struck down Sheshai, Ahiman and Talmai at Hebron (Judges 1:10). Hebron ends up in Caleb's hands.
